Assignment Title: Employee Salary Calculation Using Abstract Class

Assignment Question:
Employee Salary Calculation Using Abstract Class
A company wants to calculate the monthly salary of its employees. The company has different types of employees, such as permanent employees and contract employees. Since every employee has common information such as employee ID, employee name, and basic salary, an abstract class named Employee is designed with data members employeeId, employeeName, and basicSalary. The abstract class contains a concrete method displayDetails() to display the employee information and an abstract method calculateSalary() to calculate the final salary according to the employee type. A class named PermanentEmployee extends Employee and calculates salary by adding a fixed allowance of 20% of the basic salary. Another class named ContractEmployee extends Employee and calculates salary by adding a fixed allowance of 10% of the basic salary. The program should create the appropriate employee object based on the employee type and display the employee details and calculated salary.
Class Design
Abstract Class: Employee
Data Members: employeeId, employeeName, basicSalary
Methods:
·       Employee(int employeeId, String employeeName, double basicSalary) – constructor
·       void displayDetails() – displays employee details
·       abstract double calculateSalary() – calculates the final salary
Class: PermanentEmployee
Methods:
·       calculateSalary() – returns basic salary + 20% allowance
Class: ContractEmployee
Methods:
·       calculateSalary() – returns basic salary + 10% allowance
Input Validation Conditions
The following validation rules must be satisfied:
1.    Employee ID must be greater than 0.
2.    Employee name must not be empty.
3.    Basic salary must be greater than 0.
4.    Employee type must be either 1 or 2.
           1 represents Permanent Employee.
              2 represents Contract Employee.
If any validation condition fails, the program should display Invalid Input.

An abstract class is like a template or a partially complete class. It defines what methods a class should have, but doesn't provide implementations for all of them.

In your case:

Vehicle is abstract, meaning it's incomplete - it can't exist on its own
It has an abstract method start() - this means any subclass MUST provide an implementation for this method
It has a concrete method stop() - this is already implemented
When you write Vehicle v = new Vehicle(), you're trying to create an actual object from something that's designed to be incomplete. That's not allowed in Java.

To properly use an abstract class, you need to:

Create a concrete subclass that extends the abstract class
Implement all abstract methods in that subclass
Then instantiate the concrete subclass
This is a fundamental concept in object-oriented programming - abstract classes define contracts that subclasses must fulfill. what final code should i use
